quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, what happens to stopping distance?

options.text: Stopping will be easier than without a sidecar.
Stopping will take longer than without a sidecar.
You cannot stop.
Stopping is about the same as without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer than without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. Extra weight requires more braking force to stop. Stopping also takes longer when going downhill. Together, these factors make stopping much longer with a sidecar.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Most conflicts happen at intersections. Other vehicles may cross in front of you. Stay alert at intersections and watch for vehicles that might block your path.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a road with good traction, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear brake locks on a road with good traction, keep it locked. As long as your motorcycle stays upright and travels straight, you can still control it even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: If a driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry about it.
Change lanes safely and let them pass.
Speed up.
Leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes safely and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes safely if possible. Speeding up may only make them follow even closer and faster.

questions.question: When making a turn, how much traction is available for braking?

options.text: Less traction is available for stopping.
More traction is available for stopping.
Stopping is the same as on a straight road.
You should never try to stop while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less traction is available for stopping.
questions.explanation: When leaning to turn, your tires use grip for the turn. This leaves less grip for braking. You can brake while turning, but be very careful. Some of your traction is already being used to turn.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders close while staying safe?

options.text: In pairs
In a staggered formation
In a single-file line
In a passing formation

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group tight while giving each rider safe space. Use a single-file line when turning, in curves, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another motorcycle.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider stop other drivers from sharing their lane?

options.text: Give other drivers dirty looks
Ride in the center of your lane
Ride in the left part of your lane
Ride in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves little space on either side. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share your lane with you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what speed limit applies?

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may finish a pass in a no-passing zone if you started before the zone.
You may exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow the posted speed limit. Passes are only allowed in areas where passing is permitted.

questions.question: Why should loads be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
A high load may block your view.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A high load raises your motorcycle's center of gravity. This makes your motorcycle harder to balance and control.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Use your turn signal when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others, use turn signals, keep safe space around you, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready for changes in traffic conditions.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay on the right side of your lane.
Stay on the left side of your lane.
Look to your left often.
Use your rearview mirrors more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay away from them. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. Staying on the left side of your lane gives you more distance from the parked cars.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.
Ride under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This way you can react faster to hazards.

questions.question: To stop quickly, it is best to:

options.text: Reduce engine speed and use the front brake.
Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes together.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should only be used on slippery roads.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use when used correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Take only a few minutes.
Take more than an hour.
Be complicated to do.
Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Use your high beam, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your following distance.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam headlight unless you are following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Always press on the left handgrip.
Always press on the right handgrip.
Press on the handgrip opposite the turn direction.
Press on the handgrip in the direction you are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press on the handgrip in the direction you are turning.
questions.explanation: To turn, a motorcycle must lean. Press on the handgrip in the direction you are turning to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:

options.text: Ride in a single-file line.
Ride in a staggered line.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: A staggered line is usually best for groups. However, switch to a single-file line when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Taking artificial stimulants.
Limiting the distance you ride in one day.
Taking frequent breaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks and avoid riding more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Do not use artificial stimulants, as they can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Happen at night.
Are caused by worn tires.
Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful with a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes involve riders who have less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Use the brakes slowly.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible.

questions.question: Is it legal to ride your motorcycle between two vehicles moving in the same direction?

options.text: No, it is illegal.
Yes, if traffic is heavy.
Yes, to help reduce traffic jams during the day.
Yes, if you feel comfortable doing it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot pass between two moving vehicles on a multi-lane highway or one-way street. It is illegal.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect your riding ability?

options.text: Before you reach the legal limit.
Once you reach the legal limit.
Just after the legal limit.
Well above the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you reach the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Your riding skills become impaired before you reach the legal limit.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ likely to die in a crash than riders with helmets.

options.text: Half as
Twice as
Three times as
Just as

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets. This is true at all speeds.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Give you an escape route.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to improve safety. It should keep you out of blind spots, help you see and be seen, help you avoid hazards, avoid wind from other vehicles, and give you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers do not try to share your lane.
